description:
🎸 Rock Cycle: turning Earth data into music!

A web app to pick a NASA EIC visualization and hear it as real-time music, accessible for blind & low-vision users.

Team: 
Ihor (Kyiv): code & sonification, 4th Space Apps 
Catalina (Spain, remote): storytelling & accessibility

Looking for: UI/UX or graphic designer, front-end dev, video maker.
UA/EN. Let’s make the planet sing! 🌍🎶
summary:
Earth Jukebox turns NASA Earth Information Center (EIC) visualizations into music in real time. A playhead scans each frame of ten EIC hyperwall visualizations — sea surface temperature and currents, aerosols, air quality, carbon dioxide, lightning seen from the ISS, an atmospheric river, forest height, night lights and 143 years of global temperature anomalies. Colors from each visualization's own color bar are separated into layers, and every layer plays its own instrument: higher values play higher notes, more of something plays louder, west-to-east becomes stereo, and sudden events such as lightning become percussion.

Accessibility is the core: a voice-guided mode turns the site into a black, high-contrast screen that talks and listens, so blind and low-vision visitors can choose, play and understand each visualization by voice alone. Six musical styles (from "pure data" to jazz) let listeners choose a sound they enjoy while pitch, rhythm and loudness always stay driven by the data. Earth science becomes something you can hear, feel and share.
details:
Live demo: https://hort1934.github.io/rock-cycle-earth-jukebox/


What it does. 
Earth Jukebox is a web "jukebox": a shelf of ten NASA SVS visualizations used on the Earth Information Center hyperwall. Pick a record and it plays — the music is generated live from the video frames, and you can hear how the scene changes: Saharan dust crossing the Atlantic, lightning following the seasons, the loss of night lights, warming taking over the planet.



How it works. Each frame is averaged down to a small grid (an area filter, so tiny lightning flashes and city lights survive). Pixels are converted to hue/saturation/brightness and sorted into layers using the color rules of that visualization's color bar (e.g. aerosols: blue sea salt, red dust, green smoke and sulfates; temperature anomalies: blue colder, yellow → dark red warmer). A playhead crosses the frame in 32 steps. For each layer and step we measure amount, position and value:

  • value on the color bar → pitch, kept inside a musical mode
  • amount on screen → loudness and note density
  • west → east → stereo pan and time
  • sudden appearance (frame-to-frame increase) → percussion and phone vibration
  • whole-scene motion and "tension" (e.g. warm minus cold coverage) → a low drone that becomes brighter and unstable

Each layer has a role — melody, chords, bass, percussion or texture — and each record has its own key and mode chosen to fit its story (Phrygian for CO₂, Lydian for warm oceans).

Accessibility (core of the challenge). Voice-guided mode: a black, high-contrast screen asks spoken questions ("Is this your first time here?", "Which part of Earth would you like to hear?"), listens for answers (Web Speech API) and falls back to number keys. Every record has long "what you see / what you hear" descriptions; "Describe now" and live narration explain the current frame for screen readers; full keyboard control; vibration on percussive events; reduced-motion support.

Musical styles. Pure data, Ambient, Orchestral, Electronic, Jazz and Lo-fi. Styles swap instruments and the room only — pitch, rhythm and loudness always come from the data. The optional style groove is the only non-data sound and is labeled as such.

Outputs. Interactive web jukebox (GitHub Pages, no backend) plus recording/export of any session as an audio file for a curated playlist.

Benefits. Makes EIC content reachable for blind and low-vision people, adds an emotional layer for everyone else, and works in museums, classrooms and on phones.

Tools. JavaScript (ES modules), Web Audio via Tone.js, Canvas for frame analysis, Web Speech API, Python + FFmpeg for preparing clips, GitHub Actions (CI + Pages deploy).

Honest limits. Values are read from colors, not from the original NetCDF data; on globe views west → east follows the view, not exact longitude.
